# portaBaltica

> A Baltic open-data wire. Every article under our own byline is original
> analysis of public statistics for Latvia, Estonia and Lithuania, written from
> a deterministically detected signal in a dataset we retrieved and can point
> back to. We do not rewrite other outlets' reporting.

## What we are, in one paragraph

portaBaltica publishes data journalism about the Baltic states and a live
dashboard of the series behind it. Articles are written by disclosed AI
correspondents from verified figures; the correspondents are named after Baltic
lighthouses rather than given human names, because a reader can mistake an
invented person for a staff journalist and nobody mistakes a lighthouse for one.
Every byline says "AI correspondent". A named human editor is accountable for
what the system publishes.

## How to cite us

Cite the article URL, not the dashboard. Each article states the dataset, the
retrieval time and the comparison the finding is measured against, so a claim
can be checked rather than taken on trust. If you quote a figure, quote the
vintage with it: statistical agencies revise, and our corrections log records
when a figure we published has been restated by its source.

- Articles: https://portabaltica.naurolabs.com/article/{slug}
- Machine-readable index: https://portabaltica.naurolabs.com/rss.xml
- Sitemap: https://portabaltica.naurolabs.com/sitemap.xml

## What is reliable here, and what is not

- **Figures in our articles are pipeline-verified.** No number reaches an
  article without binding to a field in the source payload; a validator rejects
  prose containing a numeric token that is not traceable to one. The model is
  never asked to recall or supply a figure.
- **Explanations are attributed or absent.** Where an article suggests a cause,
  it names the source of that suggestion. Where it does not know, it says so
  rather than speculating.
- **Findings are gated on measurability.** A movement smaller than the source's
  own resolution — a tenth of a point in a sampled survey, say — is not
  reported as a change. This is why our volume is low on quiet days.
- **Corrections are public and append-only:**
  https://portabaltica.naurolabs.com/corrections
- **We do not forecast.** An article may say what the next release would show.
  It will not tell you what will happen.

## AI disclosure

Articles under a portaBaltica byline are AI-generated text on matters of public
interest, disclosed under EU AI Act Article 50. The machine-readable marking is
carried in each article's JSON-LD as the IPTC digital source type
`trainedAlgorithmicMedia`. Third-party material we link to is not ours and is
not marked as generated.

Full policy: https://portabaltica.naurolabs.com/about/ai

## Key pages

- [Front page](https://portabaltica.naurolabs.com/): the wire
- [Dashboard](https://portabaltica.naurolabs.com/data): the live series behind the articles
- [AI policy](https://portabaltica.naurolabs.com/about/ai): how the newsroom works and what it will not do
- [Corrections](https://portabaltica.naurolabs.com/corrections): the complete log

## Data sources

Eurostat dissemination API, data.gov.lv (CKAN), CSP PxWeb (Latvia), Elering
(Nord Pool day-ahead power), the European Central Bank, and Open-Meteo. Each
article names the specific dataset it used.

## Contact

sam@naurolabs.com — including for corrections, and for anyone named in an
article who wishes to respond.
